pages.story_text: Jordan knelt on the jagged cliff. Below him, the Fire Clan village glowed like a bed of angry embers. It had taken years of searching, but he had finally found them.
Act II begins: The Rooftops path.
Act III begins at the Village Core confrontation.
Act IV begins at the mountain ascent.
Act V begins in the Sanctum of the Unbound.
Act VI alias routes to the final sanctum content.
He narrowed his eyes as the wind kicked up hot ash. The scent of woodsmoke filled the air. To anyone else, it was just a fire, but to Jordan, it was the smell of the night his world ended.
The orange glow in his eyes blurred into a memory of his own home. He saw the red banners of the Fire Clan waving through the sparks. He saw his people scattered and his village turned to gray dust.
A younger Jordan knelt in the ruins of his home. The heat was unbearable, but his heart felt cold. In that moment, surrounded by smoke, he made a silent promise to find the people who did this.

Jordan stood up from the ash. He knew that to get justice, he could not stay a frightened child. He sought out a mysterious hermit living in the frozen peaks—a man who had been exiled from the Fire Clan long ago.

Jordan climbed into the highest mountains, where the air was thin and the wind bit like a cold blade. He had heard stories of a hermit who lived in a cave made of blue ice. This man was once a great warrior of the Fire Clan before he was cast out.

Inside the cave, a man sat by a small, flickering fire. His face was covered in scars, and his eyes were as sharp as flint. "Who are you to wake an old ghost?" the Exile growled, reaching for a heavy wooden staff.

Jordan did not flinch. "My name is Jordan," he said, his voice steady. "The Fire Clan took everything from me. They burned my home and scattered my people into the wind. I have spent years looking for a way to stop them."

The Exile looked at Jordan's hands and saw the fire of revenge in his eyes. "I know the darkness of that clan better than anyone," the Exile whispered. "If you want to defeat them, you must learn to fight like them. Are you ready for years of pain?"
The Exile nodded slowly. "Then we begin," he said. "The Fire Clan has many secrets. Which path do you wish to master so you can survive the journey ahead?"
The Exile stood on a high rock and began to throw small stones at Jordan. At first, Jordan was too slow and felt the sting of every impact. "Your eyes are too slow," the Exile barked.

For years, Jordan practiced with a blindfold tied tight over his eyes. He stopped trying to "see" the stones and began to "feel" the air move. His body began to react before his mind even realized the danger.
In his final test, the Exile swung a wooden blade at Jordan’s neck with full force. Jordan did not think; he simply moved, his body a blur of motion. He was now faster than the strike of a cobra.

pages.story_text: Jordan sat beneath a freezing mountain waterfall, the heavy water crashing onto his shoulders. The cold was like thousands of tiny needles. "If you cannot control your breath, you cannot control the battle," the Exile warned.

For years, Jordan spent his nights sitting in total silence, even as the wind howled and the mountain shook. He learned to lock away his fear and his anger in a small box in his mind. Nothing could break his concentration.
The Exile lit a circle of fire around Jordan and told him to wait. As the flames roared, Jordan remained as still as a stone statue. His heart beat slow and steady, even in the face of death.

choices.label: Go to Page 14 — Preparing the Journey

pages.story_text: The Exile led Jordan to a forest of frozen bamboo and told him to strike it with his bare hands. Each hit sent a shock of pain through his arms. "To break your enemy, you must first be unbreakable," the Exile said.

For years, Jordan conditioned his body against the harshest elements. He climbed jagged rocks without shoes and carried heavy stones up the mountain peaks. His skin grew thick, and his bones became as strong as iron beams.
In the final trial, the Exile struck Jordan with a heavy wooden staff. The wood snapped in two against Jordan’s chest, but he did not move an inch. He was now a living shield.

choices.label: Go to Page 14 — Preparing the Journey

pages.story_text: The Exile hung hundreds of tiny bells from the ceiling of a dark room. Jordan’s task was to walk across without making a single sound. "If they hear you, you are already dead," the Exile whispered.

For years, Jordan practiced moving through the shadows in total silence. He learned to step only when the wind blew and to hide in shadows thinner than a blade. He became a ghost that the world forgot.
The Exile tried to track Jordan through a thick forest for an entire night. Even with his master’s sharp eyes, the Exile could not find a single footprint. Jordan had become one with the darkness.

Jordan snapped back to the present day. He was back on the cliff, the weight of his gear feeling familiar. He looked at his hands—they were strong now. The boy from the ash was gone.
The fires were bright, and guards patrolled every corner. Jordan had to choose his path carefully. One mistake would alert the entire clan. How should he enter?

choices.label: A) The Rooftops: High above the guards.
B) The Streets: Fast but dangerous.
C) The Sewers: Dirty, dark, and hidden.

pages.story_text: Jordan stood at the base of the village wall. He looked up at the jagged stone reaching toward the smoky sky. To get inside, he had to reach the wooden walkways high above the guards.
The air was thinner up here. Jordan moved across the clay tiles, his heart thumping against his ribs. Below him, Fire Clan soldiers laughed around their pits, unaware a ghost watched from above.
A single guard stood on a narrow wooden beam. He was yawning, but his spear blocked the only path forward.
Near a chimney, Jordan spotted a small iron chest marked with the Fire Master seal.

choices.label: Open with Vial of Acid / lock trick

pages.story_text: Jordan stepped into the main street. The village smelled of roasted meat and sulfur. Torches cast long shadows across the cobbles.
In a narrow side alley, Jordan found a man slumped against a crate in Fire Clan colors, bleeding badly.
A massive iron gate stood between Jordan and the inner square. Two guards waited with spears.
The air in the sewers was thick and hot. Jordan stepped into murky water. He slipped on a mossy pipe and crashed into the muck; his gear snapped against stone.
A mutated fire-lizard lunged from the dark water.
Jordan reached the exit ladder with his arm pulsing in pain. A fallen scout held a Dirty Bandage nearby.
A rusted iron grate blocked the sewer exit.

choices.label: Melt hinges with Vial of Acid (Safe)

pages.story_text: Jordan stepped into the center of the village square. The Fire Master stood waiting and flicked a kunai toward Jordan’s heart.
The Master kicked a cloud of burning ash into Jordan’s face and lunged with a lightning-fast sword strike.

choices.label: Reflex discipline: counter and injure Master

pages.story_text: The Master charged with a glowing red strike powerful enough to shatter defenses.
The Master, wounded and breathing hard, vanished in a cloud of red smoke and fled toward the volcano.
Jordan reached the mountain base. Three paths led into the darkness.
Jordan stood at the base of the volcano. Sulfur filled the air and the ground hummed as he weighed three paths.
The trail ended at a massive cliff face.
In the ash forest, two Fire Clan ninjas dropped from the branches.
Because Jordan showed mercy to the scout, he found the hidden Crow lever and entered a safe tunnel.
The paths converged at a narrow stone bridge over flowing lava.
A massive crack split the ledge outside the Master’s sanctum.
The Fire Master stood over magma and roared: "Ancient Spirit of the Flame, I offer my soul!"
A spectral white-fire entity coiled around the Master. His screams became an otherworldly laugh as his form transformed.
The spirit pulse shattered pillars. A massive shockwave ripped through the volcano toward Jordan’s crossing.
The mountain groaned as the shockwave hit.
Jordan stood in a secret chamber with a glowing Healing Spring. On an altar rested the Frost-Bitten Dagger.
Jordan stepped into the heart of the volcano. A ten-foot entity of white flame and obsidian stood where the Fire Master had been. "I am the storm that chooses where lightning falls," it boomed.
The Master appeared in three places at once, obsidian blades whistling toward Jordan’s neck.
Jordan held his stance in the heat. "Your chaos is just loud noise," he said. "I am the silence that follows."
The Master raised jagged obsidian pillars in an overlapping trap.

choices.label: Vial of Acid collapse central pillar

pages.story_text: Jordan challenged the Master: fear is why the clans followed you. The Master flared with white fire.
The Master’s arm became a plasma whip that carved voids in the air, pulling at Jordan’s movement.
The voids collapsed inward. Obsidian skin flaked from the Master, revealing terrified human eyes beneath.
The Master surrendered physical form. The volcano core compressed into a white-hot vacuum.
The vacuum broke. The withered Master wheezed: "Wind. Earth. They will fight you with the world itself."
Jordan delivered the final strike. White fire surged into him, then settled as controlled crimson flame. "The Fire Clan ends with you," he whispered.
The volcano groaned. Jordan sprinted through collapsing tunnels and burst out as the peak shattered into the ocean.
Jordan stood on black sand and raised a small Balanced Flame above his palm. Far away, a Wind Clan Dragon and Earth Clan Golem watched from a ridge. [THE END... FOR NOW]
Jordan vanished into the lava below. His journey ended in the mountain.
